questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Tips for parents keeping children happy in lockdown
Memories of childhood seaside holidays in the UK
How schools are teaching all their lessons online
Why children watch too much TV during the holidays
questions.why: Neil says they'll discuss advice for parents keeping children educated and entertained at home.

questions.q: What does Neil remember about his childhood holidays?
options: Flying abroad to France and Spain every summer
Staying at home all summer with his grandparents
Playing I-spy in the car on the way to the seaside
Going camping in the mountains with his friends
questions.why: He remembers his dad driving them to the seaside and playing I-spy with his sister.

questions.q: What challenge for parents does Georgina mention?
options: Finding enough food for the whole family every day
Helping children with difficult maths homework
Paying for expensive online classes and tutors
Keeping children busy without hours of TV or phones
questions.why: She says parents want to keep children occupied without hours of TV or mobile phones.

questions.q: What is Elizabeth O'Shea's most important piece of advice?
options: Keep children busy every minute
See the time at home as an opportunity
Let children decide everything
Follow the school timetable exactly
questions.why: She says, “The most important thing is see this as an opportunity.”

questions.q: What can parents teach children during this time, according to Elizabeth?
options: How to use computers and the internet safely
Skills for coping with difficulties in the future
How to cook healthy meals for the whole family
Foreign languages, using apps and online videos
questions.why: She says parents can teach their children amazing coping skills for dealing with future difficulties.

questions.q: What does Elizabeth O'Shea suggest instead of recreating a classroom at home?
options: Working as a team with children to decide what to do
Hiring an online tutor for a few hours every day
Letting children play video games whenever they want
Giving children short tests every day to check progress
questions.why: Georgina says it might be better to work as a team and decide together what you'd like to do.

questions.q: When does Elizabeth recommend having some quiet downtime?
options: Early in the morning
Before bedtime
Only at weekends
Usually after lunch
questions.why: She says to include a nice chunk of time, normally after lunch, for quiet reading or play.

questions.q: Why does Elizabeth mention pillow fights?
options: As a way to punish children for bad behaviour
As a fun game to fill the whole afternoon
As a good way to release stress when things go wrong
As something parents should stop before it gets rough
questions.why: She calls pillow fights 'a great way to let off steam'.
